name: Pennsylvania

benefitCategories.medical: Reasonable and necessary treatment; employer may designate panel for first 90 days; fee schedule applies
benefitCategories.temporaryTotal: 66 2/3% of wages up to max ($1,273/week 2024); 500 weeks max
benefitCategories.temporaryPartial: 66 2/3% of wage loss up to max; 500 weeks
benefitCategories.permanentTotal: 66 2/3% of wages; lifetime after 500 weeks of TT exhausted if still totally disabled
benefitCategories.specificLoss: Healing period + schedule (e.g., 410 weeks for total loss of use of leg)
benefitCategories.deathBenefits: 66 2/3% of wages to dependents; 500 weeks; $11,000 burial

workersCompensation.initialClaimForm: Claim Petition (Bureau form); Notice of Compensation Payable by employer
workersCompensation.enforcementPowers: Bureau compliance investigations; penalty petitions; fraud investigation
workersCompensation.penalties: 20% penalty for unreasonable contest/delay; 50% penalty for bad faith; attorney fees

programs.name: No State Disability Insurance
programs.note: Pennsylvania has no state temporary disability insurance program

programs.name: PA Medical Assistance (Medicaid)
programs.eligibility: Low-income; Pennsylvania expanded Medicaid under ACA

programs.name: General Assistance
programs.note: GA for disabled adults was eliminated in 2019; limited SSI supplement remains

civilRightsFramework.retaliationProhibitions: Retaliation prohibited for filing complaints, testifying, or participating in proceedings

accommodationObligations.standard: Reasonable accommodation for non-job-related handicap or disability
accommodationObligations.process: Interactive process; similar to ADA framework

enablingStatutes.disability: No state TDI; 62 P.S. (Public Welfare Code)

laborStandards.agency: PA Bureau of Labor Law Compliance
laborStandards.authority: Wage Payment and Collection Law; Child Labor Law; Prevailing Wage

occupationalSafety.authority: Pennsylvania is not a state plan state; OSHA covers private sector

filingDeadlines.wcClaim: 3 years from injury (discovery rule may extend)
filingDeadlines.civilRightsLawsuit: 2 years from violation (after PHRC or without exhaustion per case law)

evidentiaryStandards.wc: Preponderance of evidence; unequivocal medical evidence often required

judicialReview.wc: WCJ → WCAB → Commonwealth Court → Supreme Court
judicialReview.civilRights: PHRC → Commonwealth Court (or direct court filing in some circumstances)
judicialReview.note: Some case law allows direct filing without PHRC exhaustion for PHRA claims

specialConsiderations.ireProvision: After 104 weeks, insurer may request Impairment Rating Evaluation; if less than 35%, may convert to partial status (Act 111 of 2018 modified original IRE provision after court ruling)
specialConsiderations.litigationRequirements: Unequivocal medical testimony often required; competing medical opinions common
specialConsiderations.utilization: Utilization Review process for medical treatment disputes
specialConsiderations.philadelphiaNotes: Philadelphia has local human relations ordinance with additional protections
